notes.summary: This chapter covers speed, distance and time, unit conversion, relative speed, trains, boats and streams, time and work, pipes and cisterns, and sharing wages. RRB NTPC and Group D typically include 2-4 such questions, and train-crossing problems are the most frequent.
keyPoints: Distance = speed × time. km/h to m/s: multiply by 5/18 (72 km/h = 20 m/s); m/s to km/h: multiply by 18/5.
Relative speed: add the speeds when moving in opposite directions, subtract when moving in the same direction. Time to cross = total distance ÷ relative speed.
A train crossing a pole, tree or standing man covers its own length; crossing a platform, bridge or another train covers the sum of the two lengths.
Boats: downstream = u + v, upstream = u − v. Still-water speed u = (down + up) ÷ 2; stream speed v = (down − up) ÷ 2.
Average speed for equal distances at x and y = 2xy ÷ (x + y); in every other case use total distance ÷ total time.
Work: if A takes a days, A does 1/a of the work per day. Together A and B take ab ÷ (a + b) days (10 and 15 days → 6 days).
For the same work: M1 × D1 × H1 = M2 × D2 × H2 (men × days × hours per day).
Pipes: inlets add, leaks/outlets subtract. If a pipe fills in x hours but takes y hours with a leak, the leak alone empties it in xy ÷ (y − x) hours.
Wages are shared in the ratio of work done; when people work for the same days, that is the inverse ratio of their individual times (10 days and 15 days → 3 : 2).
Late/early problems: the difference between the two travel times = late minutes + early minutes.
traps: Forgetting to convert km/h to m/s when lengths are in metres and time is in seconds.
Using only the train's length when it crosses a platform or another train.
Taking the simple average of two speeds for a journey with equal distances.
Sharing wages in the ratio of days taken instead of the inverse ratio.
In late/early questions, using 10 − 5 minutes instead of 10 + 5 minutes as the time gap.
notes.examTip: In work and pipe questions, take total work as the LCM of the given times so every daily or hourly rate is a whole number.

questions.text: Two towns are 300 km apart. A car leaves one town at 40 km/h and, at the same time, a bus leaves the other town at 60 km/h, travelling towards each other. After how long will they meet?
questions.explanation:
Moving towards each other, relative speed = 40 + 60 = 100 km/h.
Time to meet = distance ÷ relative speed = 300 ÷ 100 = 3 hours.
(15 hours comes from wrongly subtracting the speeds.) Answer: 3 hours.

questions.text: A and B together can finish a piece of work in 12 days. A alone can finish it in 20 days. In how many days can B alone finish the work?
questions.explanation:
B's one-day work = 1/12 − 1/20 = 5/60 − 3/60 = 2/60 = 1/30.
So B alone takes 30 days.
LCM method: total work = 60 units; A and B do 5 units/day, A does 3, so B does 2 units/day → 60 ÷ 2 = 30 days. Answer: 30 days.

questions.text: A boat goes downstream at 18 km/h and upstream at 12 km/h. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
questions.explanation:
Speed in still water = (downstream speed + upstream speed) ÷ 2.
= (18 + 12) ÷ 2 = 15 km/h.
(The stream's speed is (18 − 12) ÷ 2 = 3 km/h.) Answer: 15 km/h.

questions.text: Two trains of lengths 140 m and 160 m are running on parallel tracks in opposite directions at 60 km/h and 48 km/h. How long will they take to cross each other completely?
questions.explanation:
Opposite directions, so relative speed = 60 + 48 = 108 km/h = 108 × 5/18 = 30 m/s.
Distance to cover = sum of lengths = 140 + 160 = 300 m.
Time = 300 ÷ 30 = 10 seconds. Answer: 10 seconds.

questions.text: A train 250 m long is running at 50 km/h. In how much time will it pass a man who is walking at 5 km/h in the same direction as the train?
questions.explanation:
Same direction, so relative speed = 50 − 5 = 45 km/h = 45 × 5/18 = 12.5 m/s.
Distance = length of the train = 250 m.
Time = 250 ÷ 12.5 = 20 seconds.
(18 seconds comes from ignoring the man's speed.) Answer: 20 seconds.

questions.text: A train crosses a pole in 15 seconds and a 100 m long platform in 25 seconds. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanation:
The extra 25 − 15 = 10 seconds is the time taken to cover the platform's 100 m.
Speed = 100 ÷ 10 = 10 m/s.
Length of train = speed × time to cross the pole = 10 × 15 = 150 m. Answer: 150 m.

questions.text: A pipe can fill a tank in 8 hours. Because of a leak at the bottom, it takes 10 hours to fill the tank. In how many hours can the leak alone empty the full tank?
questions.explanation:
Leak's emptying rate = filling rate without the leak − net rate with the leak.
= 1/8 − 1/10 = 5/40 − 4/40 = 1/40 of the tank per hour.
So the leak empties the full tank in 40 hours.
Shortcut: (8 × 10) ÷ (10 − 8) = 40. Answer: 40 hours.

questions.text: 18 men working 6 hours a day can complete a piece of work in 20 days. In how many days will 15 men working 8 hours a day complete the same work?
A can do a piece of work in 10 days and B can do it in 15 days. They work together and receive ₹2,500 for the whole work. What is A's share?
questions.explanation:
Wages are shared in the ratio of work done. Working the same number of days, this is the ratio of their one-day work.
A : B = 1/10 : 1/15 = 3 : 2.
A's share = 3/5 × 2,500 = ₹1,500.
(₹1,000 comes from wrongly using the ratio 10 : 15.) Answer: ₹1,500.

questions.text: A can complete a piece of work in 15 days and B in 20 days. They work together for 4 days, after which A leaves. In how many more days will B finish the remaining work?
questions.explanation:
Take total work = LCM(15, 20) = 60 units. A does 4 units/day and B does 3 units/day.
In 4 days together they do 4 × 7 = 28 units.
Remaining work = 60 − 28 = 32 units.
B alone takes 32 ÷ 3 = 10 2/3 days.
(14 2/3 days is the total time including the first 4 days.) Answer: 10 2/3 days.

questions.text: If a student walks from home to school at 4 km/h, he reaches 10 minutes late. If he walks at 5 km/h, he reaches 5 minutes early. What is the distance from his home to the school?
questions.explanation:
Difference between the two travel times = 10 min late + 5 min early = 15 minutes = 1/4 hour.
d/4 − d/5 = 1/4, so d/20 = 1/4 and d = 5 km.
Check: 5 km at 4 km/h takes 75 min and at 5 km/h takes 60 min, a gap of 15 min. Answer: 5 km.
